clue.text: Sir Henry — m-music maker?

parts.note: the stammered 'm-' supplies the letter itself
an organ is an instrument that makes music

explanation.surface: A stuttering question about whether a knight called Sir Henry is a m-music maker.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Henry Morgan was the Welsh buccaneer, later Lieutenant Governor of Jamaica; the stutter 'm-' gives the extra M.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Henry Morgan was the famous seventeenth-century privateer, so his surname answers the knight's name.

clue.text: Mum managed to cover fastener with almond paste

parts.note: ma is mum

indicators.note: to cover says the managed letters wrap round the fastener

parts.note: ran means managed, as a business
a zip is a fastener

explanation.surface: Mother managed to coat something with almond paste.
explanation.definitionFit: Marzipan is a sweet confection of ground almonds and sugar, an almond paste.

clue.text: Coming in together at a plangent sound from drum

indicators.note: in says the answer sits within the phrase together at a plangent

explanation.surface: Musicians join together for a resonant sound from the drum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming' is a link; the letters run across 'togetheR AT A PLANgent'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rataplan is an imitative word for a beating drum, a rat-a-tat.

clue.text: Clever representation of statue

indicators.note: representation of says the letters of statue are presented in another form

explanation.surface: A clever depiction of a sculpture.
explanation.definitionFit: Astute means shrewd and quick-witted, synonymous with clever.

clue.text: Plant needing a container like this?

parts.note: a can is a tin container
thus means in this way, like this

explanation.surface: A gardening question: does this plant need to be grown in a pot?
explanation.definitionFit: Acanthus is a Mediterranean genus of plants with spiny leaves, the model for Corinthian capitals.

clue.text: Most curious about one that is surpassingly uproarious

indicators.note: about says the curious word goes round the one

parts.note: nosiest means most inquisitive
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The most inquisitive person around is also the loudest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is' is a link. 'curious' means inquisitive here, not strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisiest is the superlative of noisy, so loudest, which surpassingly uproarious describes.

clue.text: A warm place, though hard, this planet

parts.note: H is hard, as on pencils
the Earth is our planet

explanation.surface: A remark that somewhere warm can be found, though our world is hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearth is the floor of a fireplace, a warm spot in a home.

clue.text: Lampoon South African flag?

parts.note: SA is South Africa or African
to flag is to tire, to grow weary

explanation.surface: A question whether a South African banner mocks someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' looks like a banner but is a verb: to weaken or tire.
explanation.definitionFit: A satire ridicules its target, just as a lampoon mocks someone.

clue.text: Go round to view ring in royal gallery

indicators.note: the ring is placed in among the royal and gallery letters

parts.note: the Tate is the London art gallery
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: An invitation to tour a royal gallery to see a ring on show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to view' is only a link. The TATE is a famous London art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: To rotate is to turn or spin about a centre, going round and round.

clue.text: Snake gets on wrong train, one hopes

parts.note: the asp is a venomous snake

indicators.note: wrong signals that the letters of train are put in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A snake boards the wrong train, which is what someone hopes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets on' is only a link, and 'one hopes' is the definition, a noun phrase for a hopeful person rather than a wish.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspirant is a person with ambitions, someone who hopes to achieve something.

clue.text: A win to good man in opposition

parts.note: to gain is to win
ST, saint, is a good man

explanation.surface: A victory goes to a virtuous man who stands in opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Against means opposed to or contrary, standing in opposition.

clue.text: Extra-terrestrial one taking leave, after 'mischief doer makes complaint

indicators.note: after means the alien and the rest follow the mischief doer in the word

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous sprite
ET is the film alien, an extra-terrestrial
the Roman numeral I is one
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: An alien takes leave after a mischief-maker lodges a complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' is a medical one here, not a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetigo is a contagious skin infection, a complaint in the medical sense of ailment.

clue.text: Acrimonious marsh bird, tailless

indicators.note: tailless says the last letter of the bird's name is cut off

parts.note: the bittern is a heron of reedbeds and marshes

explanation.surface: A description of a cross marsh bird missing its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailless' drops the last letter, N, from BITTERN.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitter feelings are resentful and harsh, the same as acrimonious ones.

clue.text: Flight director?

parts.note: not a person running an airline but a hinged part of a wing that steers an aircraft in flight

explanation.surface: Someone in charge of air travel.
explanation.definitionFit: Ailerons are hinged flaps on wings that control an aircraft's roll and so its course.

clue.text: Mingled with a zodiac sign it is most insubstantial

indicators.note: mingled means the letters of the sign and it are mixed together into a new order

parts.note: Aries, the Ram, is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Astrology talk: mixed with a star sign, it becomes something very flimsy.
explanation.walkthrough: The star sign has to be worked out before 'Mingled' can mix it with the word it.
explanation.definitionFit: Airiest is the superlative of airy, meaning lightest and least solid, so most insubstantial.

clue.text: Contracted to get brigade redeployed across Land's End

indicators.note: across says the redeployed letters lie over the one taken from the end
redeployed means the letters of brigade are moved into new positions
End picks the last letter of the word Land's

explanation.surface: A brigade is moved across the tip of Cornwall, cut down in size.
explanation.walkthrough: Land's End is the westernmost point of Cornwall, but here 'End' takes D, the final letter of 'Land'. BRIGADE rearranged as ABRIGED goes around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Abridged means shortened or condensed, as a contracted text is.

clue.text: Princess's hushed restlessness?

parts.note: Di's, Princess Diana's
quiet means hushed

explanation.surface: Princess Diana kept quiet but was uneasy.
explanation.walkthrough: DI is Princess Diana.
explanation.definitionFit: Disquiet is anxiety or unease, a state of restlessness.

clue.text: A call for help to bury top — hazardous material

indicators.note: to bury says the distress call surrounds the word for top

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal
to top is to best, to beat

explanation.surface: A distress call to bury something dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' is a verb: to best someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestos is a fibrous mineral once used in insulation, now a known health danger.

clue.text: Scholar locked in an outhouse, embarrassed

indicators.note: locked in says the scholar is shut inside the outhouse letters

parts.note: a shed is an outhouse, with the article giving A
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate scholar

explanation.surface: A scholar is shut in an outbuilding and feels foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: Abashed means ashamed or disconcerted, which is what being embarrassed is.

clue.text: See
Embargo on a North American fruit

parts.note: a ban is an embargo
NA abbreviates North America

explanation.surface: A trade embargo on an American fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A banana is the long yellow fruit of a tropical plant.

clue.text: New cigar — about a pound — it's very pungent

indicators.note: about says the reworked letters go round the pound sign
new means the letters of cigar are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: L, from libra, is a pound

explanation.surface: A new cigar costing about a pound has a strong smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' turns CIGAR into GARIC, which goes 'about' L, the pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Garlic is a bulb with a strong smell and taste, notably pungent.

clue.text: Came out and attacked

explanation.surface: Someone emerged and then launched an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers who came out went on strike, and to have attacked someone is to have hit them.

clue.text: Tree yielding one current after another — a very good. return!

indicators.note: after places the second current immediately following the first

parts.note: AC is alternating current
another current, so AC again

indicators.note: return says the letters for very good are read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-class, very good, written AI

explanation.surface: A tree that produces one electric current after another and gives a great yield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a very good' is A1, written AI; 'return' turns it to IA. 'yielding' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Acacias are thorny trees and shrubs of warm countries, also called wattles.

clue.text: Hygiene problem approved quite unusual in such a' shop

parts.note: BO is body odour
U is the film certificate for universal, approved for all

indicators.note: unusual says the letters of quite are rearranged

explanation.surface: Body odour gets passed as acceptable in a fancy shop, which is unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' turns QUITE into TIQUE; U is the British film rating meaning suitable for all.
explanation.definitionFit: A boutique is a small fashionable store, a kind of shop.

clue.text: Alcoholic drinks corn product and expires

parts.note: bran is the husk left from milling grain
to die is to expire

explanation.surface: A list of things at a farm: spirits, grain by-products and death.
explanation.definitionFit: Brandies are spirits distilled from wine, so alcoholic drinks.

clue.text: Symbolic tale puts everybody on line, self included

indicators.note: included says the self is put inside the other pieces

parts.note: all means everybody
RY is railway, a line
the ego is the self

explanation.surface: Someone puts everyone on the line and includes themselves too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'line' is RY, an abbreviation for railway; EGO goes between ALL and RY.
explanation.definitionFit: An allegory is a story whose characters and events stand for deeper meanings.

clue.text: Youngster to sit (fidgeting) for painter

parts.note: a cub is a young animal or junior scout

indicators.note: fidgeting means the letters of sit move about

explanation.surface: A child made to sit still, fidgeting, for a portrait painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Youngster' points to a child sitting for a portrait, but it means a young animal or junior scout; the painter belongs to the art movement.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cubist is an artist of the movement led by Picasso and Braque.

clue.text: Chance of involving fish in stress

indicators.note: in says the fish goes inside the stress

parts.note: accent is stress on a syllable
the id or ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: The likelihood of fish being involved when someone is under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: The fish is the id, another spelling of ide, a carp-like European fish. 'of involving' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: An accident is something that happens by chance, unplanned.

clue.text: Sports equipment takes off: on fifth of August

indicators.note: off means the letters of takes are out of order
fifth of picks the fifth letter of the month's name

explanation.surface: Sports kit goes off on holiday on the fifth of August.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' turns TAKES into SKATE; S is the fifth letter of AUGUST.
explanation.definitionFit: Skates, ice or roller, are equipment used in skating sports.
